message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of calcium-containing foods:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are the most concentrated and best-absorbed sources of calcium:

- **Milk**: Nonfat milk ~299-325 mg per cup; whole milk ~276-300 mg per cup
- **Yogurt**: Plain low-fat ~415-448 mg per 8 oz; fruit low-fat ~344 mg per 8 oz
- **Cheese**: 
  - Mozzarella (part-skim) ~222-333 mg per 1-1.5 oz
  - Cheddar ~201-306 mg per 1.5 oz
  - Ricotta (part-skim) ~337 mg per 1/2 cup
  - Cottage cheese (1% fat) ~69-138 mg per 1/2 cup to 1 cup
- **Frozen yogurt**: ~103 mg per 1/2 cup
- **Ice cream**: ~85 mg per 1/2 cup

## Fish (with Bones)

- **Sardines** (canned in oil with bones): ~324-325 mg per 3 oz
- **Salmon** (pink, canned with bones): ~181 mg per 3 oz
- **Pilchards** (in tomato sauce): ~250 mg per 100g

## Plant-Based and Fortified Foods

### Fortified Beverages
- **Calcium-fortified orange juice**: ~349 mg per cup
- **Fortified almond milk**: ~482 mg per cup
- **Fortified soy milk**: ~299-399 mg per cup
- **Fortified rice milk**: ~300 mg per cup

### Soy Products
- **Tofu** (firm, made with calcium sulfate): ~253-553 mg per 1/2 cup to 1/4 block
- **Edamame** (cooked): ~130 mg per cup
- **Soybeans** (cooked): ~131 mg per 1/2 cup

### Dark Leafy Greens
- **Collard greens** (cooked): ~268-324 mg per cup
- **Kale** (cooked): ~94-177 mg per cup; raw ~24-90 mg per cup
- **Bok choy** (Chinese cabbage): ~74-158 mg per cup
- **Turnip greens** (boiled): ~99 mg per 1/2 cup
- **Spinach** (boiled): ~123 mg per 1/2 cup (but low absorption due to oxalic acid)

### Other Vegetables
- **Broccoli**: ~21-62 mg per 1/2 cup to 1 cup
- **Okra** (stir-fried): ~220 mg per 100g

### Nuts and Seeds
- **Chia seeds**: ~76-179 mg per 1 tablespoon to 1 ounce
- **Almonds**: ~76 mg per ounce
- **Sesame seeds/tahini**: ~64 mg per tablespoon
- **Brazil nuts**: ~45 mg per ounce

### Legumes and Beans
- **Baked beans**: ~53-60 mg per 1/2 cup
- **Navy beans**: ~63 mg per 1/2 cup
- **Red kidney beans** (canned): ~71 mg per 100g
- **Chickpeas**: ~40 mg per 1/2 cup

### Fruits
- **Dried figs**: ~54-250 mg per 4 figs or 100g
- **Oranges**: ~47-65 mg per medium fruit
- **Blackberries**: ~42 mg per cup
- **Dried apricots**: ~73-250 mg per 100g

### Other Foods
- **Fortified breakfast cereals**: ~100-1,000 mg per serving (varies widely)
- **Bread** (especially white/enriched): ~30-177 mg per slice or 100g
- **Tortillas** (corn): ~42-46 mg per 6" tortilla; flour tortillas ~90 mg per 10"
- **Whey protein**: ~485 mg per 100g

## Important Notes on Absorption

- Calcium absorption from **dairy products and fortified foods** is about **30%**
- Some plant foods contain **oxalic acid** (spinach, chard, collard greens, sweet potatoes, rhubarb, beans), which binds calcium and reduces absorption significantly
- **Broccoli, kale, and bok choy** have calcium bioavailability similar to milk because they contain lower levels of oxalic acid
- **Vitamin D** is essential for proper calcium absorption

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
4. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
5. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
6. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
